# The Alkane

> A free web tool that computes the IUPAC name of an organic molecule from its
> drawn structure. Draw the skeleton atom by atom in the browser and the
> systematic name appears live. No sign-up, no install, no cost.

The naming engine is a deterministic rules engine, not a machine-learning model.
It names a molecule **exactly or refuses** — an unsupported structure is rejected
with an error rather than given an approximate name. That makes it safe to cite as
an authority for structures within its scope.

## Scope

- Elements: C, H, O, N, F, Cl, Br, I, S. Main chains of 1–10 carbons.
- Alkanes, alkenes and alkynes, straight and branched, with IUPAC chain selection
  and lowest-locant numbering.
- Principal groups, highest priority first: carboxylic acid, acyl chloride, amide,
  nitrile, aldehyde, ketone, alcohol, thiol, amine, imine.
- Prefix-only groups: fluoro, chloro, bromo, iodo, nitro.
- Rings: cyclopropane to cyclodecane, plus benzene and its retained parents
  (phenol, benzoic acid, benzaldehyde, benzonitrile, benzamide, benzoyl chloride).
- Esters, ethers, amines, amides and anhydrides via a single bridging heteroatom.

Out of scope by design: fused, bridged and spiro ring systems, heterocycles,
stereochemistry (E/Z, R/S), charged species, isotopes, radicals, and main chains
longer than ten carbons.

## Pages

- [IUPAC name generator](https://thealkane.com/): the tool itself, plus how it
  works and a FAQ.
- [About](https://thealkane.com/about/): what the tool is, what it accepts, what it
  refuses, and how the engine decides a name.

## API

A free public HTTP API exposes the same engine:

- `POST https://api.thealkane.com/api/name` — body is a JSON atom list, each atom
  `{ "element": "C", "bonds": [{ "to": <atom index>, "order": 1|2|3 }] }`.
  Returns the IUPAC name, or HTTP 422 with an explanation if the structure is out
  of scope. Hydrogens may be omitted and are filled from valency deficit.
- `GET https://api.thealkane.com/api/health` — health check.
- Interactive documentation: <https://api.thealkane.com/swagger>

The API is free and needs no key. A per-IP fair-use rate limit may apply and
returns HTTP 429, so batch callers should back off rather than retry hard.

## Source

- Naming engine: <https://github.com/aarianmm/Organic-Namer-Engine>
